blocks.label: Title
blocks.text: Annual Weather Report 2026

blocks.label: Text
blocks.text: This report summarises hourly temperature, humidity and wind measurements collected across the region during the year. All sensors reported at ten minute intervals with high uptime, and no gaps longer than two hours were observed at any station in the network.

blocks.label: Title
blocks.text: 1. Overview

blocks.label: Text
blocks.text: The network now covers forty two stations spread over five provinces, up from thirty one stations a year ago. Coverage is densest in the coastal belt, where hourly readings drive the regional flood warning model, and sparsest in the highlands where power and connectivity remain limited.

blocks.label: Title
blocks.text: 3. Deployment Checklist

blocks.label: Text
blocks.text: Before the station is handed over to the regional office, the following checks must be completed and signed off by the field engineer.

blocks.label: List
blocks.text: •  Calibrate the rain gauge against the reference bucket. •  Verify the solar panel output under load for ten minutes. •  Upload the first twenty four hours of readings. •  Confirm the enclosure seal and replace any cracked gasket. •  Record the station serial number in the asset register.

blocks.label: Title
blocks.text: 4. Notes

blocks.label: Text
blocks.text: Any failed check must be reported to the regional office within two working days, together with photographs of the affected component.

blocks.label: Title
blocks.text: 5. Field Notes from the Highlands

blocks.label: Text
blocks.text: The highland route is served by six stations, three of which rely on satellite backhaul and a shared battery bank. Readings are collected twice a day by hand when the link is down.

blocks.label: Text
blocks.text: Snow cover persists from November to April, so the gauges are heated and inspected weekly. Crews report that the new mounts reduced alignment drift by half compared with 2025.

blocks.label: Title
blocks.text: 7. Sensor Calibration Log

blocks.label: Title
blocks.text: 7.1 Summary

blocks.label: Text
blocks.text: Calibration was completed for thirty eight of the forty two stations in the first quarter. The remaining four are scheduled for April, once the access road to the northern ridge is reopened.

blocks.label: List
blocks.text: •  Thirty eight stations passed on the first attempt. •  Two gauges required a replacement tipping bucket. •  One logger was swapped after a firmware fault.

blocks.text: Open items are tracked in the regional register and reviewed at the monthly operations meeting.

blocks.label: Title
blocks.text: 8. Terms of Data Use

blocks.label: Text
blocks.text: The regional office grants the receiving party a non exclusive licence to use the readings listed in the register for research and for public reporting. The licence does not extend to resale of the readings in raw form, nor to redistribution through a commercial data platform, without written consent. Attribution must name the station network and the year of collection, and must not imply that the office endorses the derived work in any way.

blocks.label: Text
blocks.text: Where readings are incomplete, the receiving party must mark the gap in the derived product and must not interpolate across it without stating the method. The office publishes a revision note when a station is recalibrated; derived products that predate the note are expected to be regenerated within one quarter, or the discrepancy stated in the accompanying documentation. Nothing in these terms transfers ownership of the raw readings, which remain the property of the station operator that recorded them in the field.

blocks.label: Text
blocks.text: Disputes are handled under the arbitration rules published with the register. The office may suspend access where a breach is not remedied within thirty days of written notice to the registered contact of the receiving party.
